_comment: Copy to fleet.json. This file is WHICH MACHINES this deployment watches.
It holds no secrets — HOST_<ID>_TOKEN in the environment supplies those —
so a private deployment repo can commit it.
kind picks the adapter: teg (Flask dashboard), agent (ojee-agent), loq (ojee-loq),
local (this machine: /proc, /sys, docker.sock), satellite (src/satellite.js on
another machine), mirror (a host as another fleet reads it).
name is what every page calls the machine (LOQ, HP, disinteg); tag is the short
identity beside it on the overview and the card (Main laptop, Home server,
Canada); role is the line under it saying what the machine is; icon picks its
glyph (i-laptop, i-server, i-cloud). hostname shows in Details.
remote lists the ojee-remote device ids that reach this machine (Screen,
Shell, Files, lock state); a dual-boot machine lists both halves and the
one that answers is the OS it is running. Needs FLEET_REMOTE_ORIGIN.
limits overrides src/normalize.js LIMITS for one host: tempWarnC/tempErrC
(colour), cpuTempC/cpuCritC/gpuTempC + heatHoldMs (heat must be HELD to
alert), diskPct, memPct, swapPct, batteryPct, latencyWarnMs/latencyErrMs (colour
of the round trip from HP; never an alert). The console's settings
(thresholds of fleet.* kinds) override every host.
mute lists alert kinds this host should never raise; muteServices names
services that are off on purpose. roaming marks a machine that LEAVES
(a laptop): when it stops answering it is away, not down.

hosts.name: LOQ
hosts.role: Lenovo LOQ · dual boot Linux/Windows · moves around

hosts.name: HP
hosts.role: Old HP laptop · lid closed, always on · runs the console

hosts.name: disinteg
hosts.role: Old desktop at a friend's house in Canada · remote
